content.comment_body: Password "[product_name]" does not work for a brand new [product_name] device.

Please avoid repeatedly quoting your own posts, as this unnecessarily extends the topic discussion. From my perspective, this issue is not due to an incorrect password. The default password remains "[product_name]". It seems more likely to be a connection issue. I am only familiar with the error message when [product_name] software communicates with the [product_name] controller and the device does not respond promptly.
Check the interface shown in your initial image, and choose an actual network connection, rather than a virtual one.
In this instance, the selected interface is incorrect!
What other options do you have available to select? If possible, try all possible interfaces. Some feedback on whether you resolve the issue would be appreciated.

analysis.insight_summary: The user had trouble accessing a new [product_name] controller using the default password '[product_name]'. However, the issue appears to stem from incorrect interface or network selection rather than an authentication problem. The discussion highlights that configuring the proper connection can be confusing for new users and may cause misinterpretation of error messages.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to connect to their new [product_name] controller using the default password easily, anticipating simple access and clear connectivity without needing complex configuration.
